title: The search space about game development principles is littered with AI slop. But here is what I don't understand:
author: EC36339
selftext:
\_Sorry for the clickbaity title, but too many people never read past the title.\_

I do most of my research with AI these days, because the traditional method is broken, and because AI gives me the right search term AND the result.

But if you DO search oldschool for something like "game collision detection" these days, you get several pages of links to nothing but slop. Articles with superficial information that is clearly AI generated on websites that are not about game development, but exist for no other purpose than attracting clicks. I don't know what their endgame is. If there are ads on those sites, I'm not seeing them.

Anyways, \*\*what I don't understand is this\*\*:

If you ask AI, even any free toy model on duck.ai, about some basics, like: "give me a crash course on bounding volumes and their shapes and acronyms and intersection tests", \*\*you usually get a good answer\*\*.

So whoever is generating those slop pages, they could at least generate content that is actually useful.

It costs nothing (as Claude would say). One simple prompt, and you get a helpful article that people who googled your shitty website might actually read, while you are showing them viagra ads or whatever your hustle is (although probably anyone smart enough to google advanced topics also knows what an ad blocker is...).

Do those slop sites float to the top on search engines BECAUSE they are slop, and the algorithm likes that, or hates anything that looks too techy or nerdy? Or are they slop on purpose, because someone in Nigeria gets a boner every time someone lands on their website and immediately hits the back button?

Would someone please enlighten me on the economics of this?

comments.author: re-skob
comments.body: I just did a google search for "game collision detection" and none of the top results were AI slop, so not sure what you're talking about

replies.author: DigitalDustChan
replies.body: Maybe OP was looking in the mirror as they wrote this

comments.body: I did the same search and all my results were real.
